admission.workflow: Evaluate static Proctor command, menu, keybinding, focus, accessibility, and workbench-routing conditions with the mature parser, normalization, implication, comparison, regex, and serialization behavior used by later workbench mechanics.

items.rationale: The canonical Microsoft MIT text is preserved as the local notice for this cluster.

Preserve the complete expression model, parser, normalization, implication, comparison, regex, serialization, metadata, and service contracts while routing fallback messages through the admitted packaged localization seam.
Preserve exact tokenization, offsets, errors, operators, quoting, regex scanning, and serialization while routing fallback messages through the admitted packaged localization seam.
VS Code's host, browser, mobile, and input context identifiers are product composition; Proctor owns its namespaced static context set and admits only keys required by its windows and capabilities.

Preserve root, scoped DOM, overlay, inherited-value, buffered-event, parent-update and deterministic disposal behavior for the executable workbench while excluding VS Code configuration-backed and inspect-command product inputs that Proctor's static namespaced context authority forbids.
Run the complete owner expression suite through Node's built-in runner and admitted Proctor paths.
Run the complete owner parser suite through Node's built-in runner and admitted Proctor paths.
Run the complete owner scanner suite through Node's built-in runner and admitted Proctor paths.

Run all fourteen applicable upstream scoped-context, reparenting, equality, buffering and disposal cases in real Chromium, with added overlay and lifecycle regressions. Only the URI-marshalling command test is omitted: generic setContext and extension commands are excluded product inputs.

Extract the complete dependency-free equals function used by Context.setValue and reparenting diffs, preserving array holes, enumerable inherited keys, null-prototype records, signed zero and NaN. Other object utilities are not dependencies of this context-key closure.

dependencies.rationale: The admitted base-common cluster supplies events, errors, platform facts, string handling, lifecycle, and character codes.
The admitted platform foundation supplies the stable context-key service identifier contract.
The private compatibility seam supplies deterministic packaged fallback messages without runtime language-pack discovery.

divergences.summary: Only Proctor-namespaced statically packaged context identifiers are product inputs; context values control presentation and routing but never authenticate, authorize, or establish authoritative Attempt or Secure Exam Posture state.

Each context forest belongs to one renderer root. Duplicate DOM scopes reject before allocation; reparenting rejects disposed scopes, foreign roots and cycles before changing ownership. Read-only overlays retain their parent's scope and inherited values during expression evaluation.

verification.obligation: Verify complete expression construction, normalization, equality, implication, evaluation, comparison, regex, serialization, and constant behavior.
Verify complete parser precedence, whitespace, operator, quoting, error, and recovery behavior.
Verify exact token types, lexemes, offsets, error cases, regex forms, and serialization.
Verify namespaced Proctor keys participate only as ordinary expression values.
Verify production root and focused-part values, scoped DOM lookup, overlays, modal changes and disposal in real Chromium.
Verify layer direction, cycles, static imports, and literal Proctor composition ownership.
Verify schema, local digest, marker, license reference, unique ownership, divergence, and evidence parity without a VS Code checkout.
Resolve the exact VS Code commit and verify every reviewed upstream blob against the canonical checkout.

Run the applicable upstream browser service suite and regressions for scoped/nested overlays, reparenting, duplicate-scope leak prevention, root/cycle guards, invalid DOM context isolation, and upstream value equality.
